record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Given a bounded region Q with connected boundary inside an asymptotically flat 3-manifold satisfying the positive mass theorem conditions, can one find an isometric extension that is static outside Q and has least ADM mass among all no-horizon extensions of Q?

evidence.quote: Let Q c (M,g) be a bounded region in a 'f 'JTI, manifold, with connected boundary. Show there is another 'f 'l1'b manifold (M* ,g*) ::> Q, isometrically, such that (M*,g*) is static outside 0 (cf. [CW]). This is part of the static metric conjecture of [BR6], which further conjectures that (M* ,g*) has least ADM mass amongst all those 'f 'JTI, extensions of Q having no horizon outside Q.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth, asymptotically flat Riemannian 3-manifold satisfying the hypotheses of the positive mass theorem (in particular, having nonnegative scalar curvature and finite ADM mass). Let $\Omega \subset (M,g)$ be a bounded region with connected smooth boundary. A no-horizon extension of $\Omega$ is a smooth asymptotically flat Riemannian 3-manifold $(M^*,g^*)$ with nonnegative scalar curvature containing $\Omega$ isometrically and admitting no closed minimal surface enclosing $\Omega$ outside $\Omega$. The manifold $(M^*,g^*)$ is said to be static outside $\Omega$ if there exists a positive function $u$ on $M^*\setminus\Omega$ satisfying the static vacuum Einstein equations $u\,\mathrm{Ric}(g^*)=\nabla^2 u$ and $\Delta u=0$ on $M^*\setminus\Omega$.

Prove or disprove: for every such $\Omega$, there exists a no-horizon extension $(M^*,g^*)$ of $\Omega$ which is static outside $\Omega$ and whose ADM mass is the infimum of ADM masses among all no-horizon extensions of $\Omega$.
artifact.status_search_result: The Bartnik static metric extension conjecture has seen significant progress but remains unresolved in general. Corvino and independently Anderson–Jauregui established that any ADM-mass minimizer among admissible extensions must be static vacuum outside Ω. However, Anderson and Khuri provided counterexamples to the most optimistic global well-posedness of the static extension boundary-value problem, and recent works (2024–2025) establish only local well-posedness near Schwarzschild spheres. Existence of the conjectured minimizing static extension for general Ω is not established.

status_evidence.title: On the Bartnik extension problem for the static vacuum Einstein equations
status_evidence.snippet: Anderson and Khuri analyze the Bartnik static extension problem and discuss obstructions/counterexamples to the most optimistic forms of the conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples exist to the strongest form of the static extension conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Existence of static vacuum extensions for Bartnik boundary data near Schwarzschild spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Local existence and well-posedness for the static extension problem is established near Schwarzschild boundary data.
status_evidence.claim: Only local results near special data have been proved; global conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: A flow approach to Bartnik's static metric extension conjecture in axisymmetry
status_evidence.snippet: Develops a geometric flow approach toward the conjecture in the axisymmetric case.
